_help: One entry per export (the packages that cannot update themselves from inside PythonOS).
api:         minimum export compatibility the CURRENT core needs. Bump it when a core change needs something the
older export lacks (a new Android bridge function, a new library, a new boot feature). Exports with a
lower api are told they must be reinstalled before the core update can be applied.
notes:       one line shown to users when they are told this export has a newer version.
assets:      release file names; {v} is the release the file was built in.
inputs:      the files/folders that end up inside the export. CI fingerprints them (OS_Export/inputs.py); if the
fingerprint matches the previous release the export is NOT rebuilt - the new release links to the old
file - and its version stays at the release it last changed in. Nothing to bump by hand.
embeds_core: true when the export contains the PythonOS core itself (the ISO), so a core change rebuilds it.
The Android, Windows and Linux packages download the core on first run, so core-only changes skip them.

extra_assets: files for other processors or formats. They are attached when they were built and never hold a release back; when an export is reused they are copied from the old release if it has them.

android.title: Android app
android.notes: New terminal screen: type straight into the terminal, always scrolled to the bottom, symbol keys, zoom.

iso.title: Bootable ISO
iso.notes: Locked down: boot menu and consoles can no longer reach the Linux system underneath.

wizard.title: Setup Wizard
wizard.notes: One program that detects your computer, asks what you want (install, Android, bootable USB, virtual machine, Docker) and gets the right file.
